summary: Partial URL and trailing markdown truncated after SSE path switch, resumed stream reorders final fragments
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a short SSE path failover (edge proxy -> alternate path) a generated URL in the final paragraph is truncated mid-host and a concluding markdown codeblock closes prematurely. When the client reconnects and the platform attempts to resume, fragments arrive out-of-order resulting in duplicated middle fragments and a later missing sentence.

Impact:
- WaveNote sees frequent user-visible truncation of generated links and malformed markdown in ~3% of long streaming responses (30–60s).
- Causes confusion in product flows that open generated URLs; some links are unusable.
- Affects customer-facing production traffic on dedicated pool in us-west.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dcp-usw-14
- API path: /v1/streams/generate (SSE)
- Model: redwood/gpt-medium-2025 pinned @ v2026-02-28
- Client: browser (Chrome 115) behind corporate edge appliance (FastEdge v2.1)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start long stream (streaming instructions with example URL and closing markdown codeblock).
2) Induce short path failover by toggling the client's corporate proxy (simulated with packet loss on port 443 for ~1.5s).
3) Client reconnects and SSE resume header is sent.
4) Observe truncated URL and premature codeblock termination in final streamed chunks.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Customer captured final stream: "https://api.wave.../open?token=eyJhbGci..."
```bash
echo 'done'
```
- Server resume negotiation trace (excerpt): "resume-offset=12456; session-id=sn-7a3d..."
- Edge proxy log: path-swap detected, keepalive gap 1350ms, rewrote chunk-size header during resend.

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge proxy path switch causes chunk boundary resegmentation; SSE resume uses byte-offsets relative to pre-swap stream so fragments are re-sent with overlapping ranges. Overlap + truncated chunk at the path boundary leads to a partial token (URL host split) being accepted and later resume fragments are applied out-of-order by the client SDK.
- Secondary factor: platform keepsalive coalescing compresses small JSON envelopes which, when split by the proxy, lose a closing backtick sequence for codeblocks in the last chunk.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Disable client-side fast-reconnect and add a 500ms randomized backoff before reconnecting to reduce overlap windows.
- Have content validated on client and retry full generation when truncated URLs are detected.

Notes / attachments:
- Provided pcap and browser console capture (customer attached).
- Link to customer's reproducer harness: https://github.com/WaveNoteInc/stream-repro (private).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:15 - Support (Maya): Received pcap and console logs; reproduced with local proxy that introduces a 1.2s stall.
2026-03-11 11:40 - SRE (Liam): Found edge-proxy log entries that rewrite Transfer-Encoding in a failover path; observed keepalive gap 1300–1500ms correlated with affected requests.

2026-03-11 13:05 - Runtime (Anika): Replayed stream at serving-runtime with deliberate chunk boundary split; confirmed behavior where final JSON event lost trailing backticks when the platform's chunker emitted a sub-100B fragment that the proxy split mid-byte-sequence.

2026-03-11 15:22 - SRE (Liam): Verified resume offset logic uses logical event offsets not content-safe boundaries for SSE; if the upstream path resegmented packets, resume may re-emit overlapping slices which client SDK merges out-of-order.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Eng (Diego): Proposed change: add a resume-safe envelope marker and server-side reassembly check that rejects overlapping resume segments (idempotent re-emit) and prefers full-event re-fetch when overlap detected.
2026-03-12 10:00 - PM (Rina): Prioritized fix as P1 for dedicated customers; prepare canary for us-west dedicated nodes after implementation.

resolution_plan:
Short term: rollout server-side stabilization that avoids emitting tiny final fragments on detected connection instability in dedicated us-west canary hosts. Client guidance: implement a 500ms jittered reconnect backoff and detect truncated URLs to trigger full retry.
Long term: implement resume-safe envelope markers and reassembly checks in serving-runtime; ensure resume offsets align to event boundaries instead of raw bytes. Add integration tests with proxy path-swap simulation.
Owners: SRE (Liam) for canary rollout, Runtime (Anika, Diego) for code changes, Support (Maya) for customer communication. Target prod rollback/rollout: 2026-03-18 (pending canary metrics).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 18:45 - Eng (Anika): Canary deployment on 3 dedicated hosts in us-west completed. Observed affected-case rate drop from 3% -> 0.2% in sampled traffic.
2026-03-13 09:00 - SRE (Liam): No regression in throughput; edge telemetry shows reduced resegmentation artifacts post-canary. Preparing global prod rollout schedule.

2026-03-13 12:20 - Support (Maya): Shared interim mitigations and suggested client backoff with WaveNote. Customer confirmed a drastic reduction in new incidents after applying client-side backoff and after canary began serving traffic.
